a.description: Compute n*n+abs(n), move its first decimal digit to the end, and return the resulting integer. A single digit is unchanged and leading zeros in the rotated representation disappear.
a.program: dup sq swap abs add decimal-digits uncons quote cat from-digits

b.description: Return the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n²+|n|. Leading zeros after reversal disappear; zero returns zero.
b.program: dup sq swap abs add decimal-digits reverse from-digits

a.description: Compute int(n==0) from the integer argument.
a.program: 0 eq? bool>int

a.description: Compute abs(n) factorial, sort its decimal digits ascending, and interpret those digits as an integer, dropping leading zeros. For n=0 the result is 1.
a.program: abs factorial decimal-digits sort from-digits

b.description: Compute abs(n)!, sort its decimal digits ascending, remove duplicates, and interpret the remaining digits as a decimal integer. Any initial zero has no numeric effect; n=0 returns 1.

a.description: Among integers 1 through abs(n), count selections a<b where a divides b and b-a is odd. For n=0 return 0; negative n uses its absolute value.

a.description: Concatenate the ordinary decimal representations of |a| and |b|, reverse all their digits, and return the resulting integer. Each zero contributes one digit.

a.description: Compute int(a==b) from the two integer arguments.

b.program: [ sq ] dip sq add palindrome? bool>int

b.description: Compute int(a==b) from the two integer arguments.

a.program: [ 0 max2 range1 ] dip 0 max2 range1 [ swap [ [ over over add odd? ] [ min2 ] [ drop drop 0 ] ifte ] swap cons map sum ] swap cons map sum

b.description: Count positive integer triples (i,j,k) with i<=max(a,0), j<=max(b,0), i+j even, and 1<=k<abs(i-j). Nonpositive bounds yield 0.
b.program: [ 0 max2 range1 ] dip 0 max2 range1 [ swap [ sub abs [ dup even? ] [ dec 0 max2 ] [ drop 0 ] ifte ] swap cons map sum ] swap cons map sum

a.description: Count selections of two distinct cells from the same row of a rectangular grid with max(a,0) rows and max(b,0) columns. The two cells are unordered; nonpositive dimensions yield 0.
a.program: [ 0 max2 ] dip 0 max2 choose2 mul

b.description: For positive selections i<=max(a,0), j<=max(b,0) of opposite parity, sum min(i,j), the number of positive k bounded by both selections. Nonpositive bounds yield 0.
b.program: [ 0 max2 range1 ] dip 0 max2 range1 [ swap [ [ over over add odd? ] [ min2 ] [ drop drop 0 ] ifte ] swap cons map sum ] swap cons map sum

limitations: Raw output equality on existing shared probes approximates similarity; it does not prove useful diversity.
Probe distribution is finite and includes repeated edge structures; list and scalar kinds have different coverage.
High modal-output probabilities and mostly constant behaviors can inflate agreement; per-type baselines and entropy are supplied.
Nearest-neighbor ties use the first row in corpus order. No generated execution, fresh probes, eval contents or model calls.
Input intersection alignment is checked against saved shared_count; saved outputs are trusted as already verified.
